Balancing area overview

Balancing areas are the regions of the Canadian electricity grid used by this model. Most provinces are a single balancing area; Newfoundland, Ontario, and Quebec are split into two. Choose an area to see where its grid cells are and how its demand varies.

Map overview

Each rectangle is one CODERS map grid cell. Cells in the selected balancing area are dark blue.

Demand overview

Annual demand

Total electricity demand in the selected balancing area for each year, in GWh.

Normalized demand

A normalized demand curve is generated for each year by dividing the demand in each hour by the average hourly demand for that year. Demand curves for each year are then averaged to produce a multi-year normalized demand. This demand curve can be used when selecting sites for renewable generation in that balancing area. This allows tailoring generation to the general demand curve, without overfitting to the demand for a particular year. The average hourly value in this graph will always be 1.0, and typically has a range between 0 and 2.0.
